definition: a small, common brown bird found in many parts of the world

collocations.example: A house sparrow built its nest under our roof last spring.
A flock of sparrows scattered when the cat crept closer.

definition: to scatter small drops of liquid over a surface

collocations.example: Frying bacon can spatter grease all over the clean stove.
The passing truck spattered mud across the windshield.

definition: to cover a surface with small spots or marks of color

collocations.example: Faint stars speckle the sky long after sunset.
Brown spots speckle the ripe pear's surface.

definition: an oval track used for motor racing with cars or motorcycles

collocations.example: Speedway racing draws huge crowds to the oval track.
The cars thundered around the speedway for forty laps.

definition: to send out something, such as smoke or liquid, in large amounts

collocations.example: Factory chimneys spew out thick smoke every single day.
The volcano began to spew lava across the valley.

definition: to splash a liquid in large drops onto a surface

collocations.example: The kids love to splatter paint on the big canvas.
He splattered paint across the canvas.

definition: to join two pieces of film, rope, or wire at their ends

collocations.example: Editors once had to splice film by hand with tape.
You can splice together short clips to make one video.

definition: the quality of being natural, unplanned, and done on impulse

collocations.example: Traveling without a plan gave the trip a sense of spontaneity.
Too much rehearsal made the performance lose its spontaneity.

definition: an injury to a joint caused by twisting it suddenly

collocations.example: She got an ankle sprain during the soccer match.
Runners often suffer a sprain on uneven ground.

definition: false or fake, though appearing to be real or genuine

collocations.example: The ad made a spurious claim about curing baldness.
They fired him on spurious grounds last month.

definition: to reject something or someone with scorn or contempt

collocations.example: They may spurn an offer that seems too generous.
He spurned every offer of help out of pride.

definition: a loud, harsh cry, especially one made by a bird

collocations.example: The parrot let out a squawk when the door slammed.
The hens scattered with an angry squawk.

definition: an adult male deer

collocations.example: A mighty stag appeared at the edge of the woods.
Hunters admired the stag's antlers from a distance.

definition: the vertical open space in a building that contains a staircase

collocations.example: The old building had a dark stairwell at the back.
He hurried down the stairwell to the exit.

definition: a situation in which no side can make progress or win

collocations.example: These talks could easily end in stalemate.
A fresh offer finally helped break the stalemate.

definition: loyal, reliable, and firm in support of a cause or group

collocations.example: She remained a stalwart supporter of the charity.
He was stalwart in his loyalty to old friends.

definition: a group of lines forming a unit in a poem

collocations.example: The opening stanza sets the mood for the poem.
Each verse is written as a four-line stanza.

definition: the right-hand side of a ship or aircraft when facing forward

collocations.example: A wave struck the starboard side of the boat.
The captain told the crew to steer to starboard.

definition: a secret store of something that is hidden away

collocations.example: Police found a stash of cash in the attic.
He kept a secret stash of candy in his desk.

definition: firm and unwavering in belief, loyalty, or purpose

collocations.example: He stayed steadfast in his belief despite the criticism.
She proved a steadfast friend through hard times.

definition: to soak something in liquid for a period of time

collocations.example: Steep the tea leaves in hot water for five minutes.
Let the dried fruit steep overnight before baking.

definition: extremely good; outstanding in quality or performance

collocations.example: The actor gave a stellar performance on opening night.
The reviews said her debut was absolutely stellar.

definition: a substance that makes the body or mind more active and alert

collocations.example: Caffeine is a powerful stimulant found in coffee.
The drug can act as a stimulant on the heart.

definition: to add fuel to a fire and make it burn more strongly

collocations.example: He paused to stoke up the dying fire.
Workers took turns to stoke the furnace all night.

definition: a rule or restriction that strictly limits what you can do

collocations.example: The budget placed tight strictures on travel spending.
The board may impose strictures on new hiring.

definition: loud and harsh

collocations.example: She silenced the room with her strident voice.
The alarm's strident ring woke the whole house.

definition: the short, stiff hairs on a man's face when he has not shaved

collocations.example: A rough growth of stubble covered his tired face.
His scratchy stubble brushed against her cheek.

definition: a type of plaster used to cover and decorate walls

collocations.example: The house had smooth white stucco walls.
The old brick was coated with stucco for protection.

definition: lacking fresh air; too warm and poorly ventilated

collocations.example: The crowded, stuffy room made breathing difficult.
The attic gets hot and stuffy in the summer.

definition: to stop something or someone from growing or developing fully

collocations.example: Crowded roots will stunt its growth over time.
Too little funding can stunt development here.

definition: to bring a people or country under control, usually by force

collocations.example: The general set out to subjugate a nation by force.
Conquerors always seek to subjugate the lands they invade.

definition: a legal document ordering someone to appear in a court of law

collocations.example: Officers arrived to serve a subpoena on the witness.
The committee voted to issue a subpoena for records.

definition: too ready to obey others; treated as less important

collocations.example: The press should not be subservient to the government.
She refused to accept a subservient role at work.

definition: to include something within a larger group or category

collocations.example: These small teams were subsumed under one department.
The old firm was subsumed into a global group.

definition: existing or happening under the surface of the ground

collocations.example: Explorers found a subterranean passage under the castle.
Subterranean water slowly shaped these deep caves.

definition: soft leather with a slightly rough, velvety surface

collocations.example: He wore a brown suede jacket to the party.
The boots were made of soft gray suede.

definition: a man who wants to marry or form a romantic relationship with a woman

collocations.example: Her persistent suitor sent flowers every day.
A princess might reject a suitor she dislikes.

definition: a king or ruler in certain Muslim countries

collocations.example: Guards stood at the sultan's palace gate.
A powerful sultan once ruled these desert lands.

definition: a tall plant with a large flower of yellow petals around a dark center

collocations.example: She snacked on roasted sunflower seeds all afternoon.
We photographed a field of sunflowers at dawn.

definition: able to carry electricity with no resistance, usually at very low temperatures

collocations.example: The scanner relies on a powerful superconducting magnet.
This superconducting material carries current with no loss.

definition: more than is needed or wanted; unnecessary

collocations.example: The report was full of superfluous detail.
His long introduction felt entirely superfluous.

definition: a star that suddenly explodes and becomes extremely bright

collocations.example: A supernova explosion can outshine a whole galaxy.
Astronomers detected light from a distant supernova.

definition: believing that certain events bring good or bad luck without any real cause

collocations.example: Many people hold a superstitious belief about mirrors.
She is superstitious about walking under ladders.

definition: an extra amount of money added to the usual price or charge

collocations.example: The airline added a fuel surcharge to each ticket.
The bank may impose a surcharge for late payment.

definition: to guess something based on little evidence

collocations.example: We can surmise that he left in a hurry.
With so few clues, we can only surmise the truth.

definition: done quietly and secretly to avoid being noticed

collocations.example: She stole a surreptitious glance at her watch.
The burglar made a surreptitious entry through the window.

definition: a very confident, sometimes arrogant, way of walking or behaving

collocations.example: She crossed the stage with a confident swagger.
After the defeat he seemed to lose his swagger.

definition: to hit something, especially an insect, with a quick blow

collocations.example: She tried to swat a fly near the window.
Use your hand to swat away the bugs.

definition: to move a card through a reader, or a finger across a screen

collocations.example: You must swipe a card to open the gate.
Swipe left to see the next photo on your phone.

definition: to make two or more things happen at the same time or rate

collocations.example: The dancers tried to synchronize with the music.
The soldiers paused to synchronize watches before leaving.

definition: an official meeting of church leaders to discuss matters of religion

collocations.example: The bishops met for the annual church synod.
Leaders decided to convene a synod over the dispute.

definition: a serious disease that spreads through sexual contact

collocations.example: A person can contract syphilis through sexual contact.
Doctors use antibiotics to treat syphilis today.

definition: relating to or using the sense of touch

collocations.example: Soft velvet gives a pleasant tactile sensation.
The fabric is soft and highly tactile.

definition: a sudden change to a completely different subject or line of thought

collocations.example: He tends to go off on a tangent in meetings.
Her comment was a complete tangent from the topic.

definition: crying or about to cry

collocations.example: They shared a tearful goodbye at the airport.
She became tearful as the sad music played.

definition: relating to the structure and movement of the earth's crust

collocations.example: Earthquakes occur when tectonic plates grind together.
The region shows frequent tectonic activity.

definition: to be full of or crowded with living things

collocations.example: The tropics teem with countless insect species.
We pushed through the crowds of a teeming market.

definition: to move or balance unsteadily, as if about to fall

collocations.example: One misstep could make him teeter on the edge.
Watch the stack of books teeter back and forth.

definition: able to be defended against criticism or objection

collocations.example: Few experts think it is a tenable position.
That old idea is no longer tenable today.

definition: holding firmly to something, or refusing to give up

collocations.example: She is a tenacious negotiator who never backs down.
She was tenacious in pursuing her dream.

definition: to formally offer or present something, such as a resignation

collocations.example: She may tender a resignation if things worsen.
Three firms will tender a bid for the contract.

definition: a large, often run-down building divided into cheap apartments

collocations.example: They grew up in a run-down tenement building.
Whole families lived in one crowded tenement.

definition: a seabird like a small gull, with long wings and a forked tail

collocations.example: The Arctic tern flies enormous distances each year.
A flock of terns circled above the harbor.

definition: any of several small, lively, and energetic breeds of dog

collocations.example: Their bull terrier chased the ball across the lawn.
The lively terrier barked at every passing car.

definition: using few words, sometimes in a way that seems rude

collocations.example: He gave a terse reply and left the room.
Her emails are always terse and businesslike.

definition: third in order, rank, or level of importance

collocations.example: Many students pursue tertiary education after high school.
The tertiary sector includes banking and tourism.

definition: a formal written or spoken statement praising someone or something

collocations.example: Her boss wrote her a glowing testimonial.
The site shows a customer testimonial on each page.

definition: a device that automatically controls the temperature of a room or machine

collocations.example: She set the thermostat to a cozy temperature.
A faulty thermostat left the office freezing cold.

definition: a wild plant with prickly leaves and purple flowers

collocations.example: Some people take milk thistle to support the liver.
He pricked his hand on a prickly thistle.

definition: a handle used to turn the rudder and steer a small boat

collocations.example: You must hold the tiller firmly in rough water.
Push the tiller gently to steer around the buoy.

definition: making you feel bored, annoyed, or impatient

collocations.example: Sorting old files is a tiresome task.
The work grew tiresome and repetitive by noon.

definition: a strong, light, silver-gray metal used in industry

collocations.example: The bike frame uses a light titanium alloy.
The surgeon fitted a joint made of titanium.

definition: a thin, flat round bread made from corn or wheat flour

collocations.example: She wrapped the beans in a warm corn tortilla.
He prefers a soft flour tortilla for burritos.

definition: a very young child

collocations.example: A tiny tot toddled toward the slide.
The class is full of tots and toddlers.

definition: a large, open bag used for carrying things

collocations.example: She packed her books into a large tote bag.
He carried groceries in a sturdy canvas tote.

definition: an animal or object treated as a symbol of a family, tribe, or group

collocations.example: The carved totem pole stood near the village.
The eagle was the clan's sacred family totem.

definition: crossing or involving both sides of the Atlantic Ocean

collocations.example: They booked a transatlantic flight to London.
Transatlantic trade boomed in the nineteenth century.

definition: to make someone unable to move because of amazement or fear

collocations.example: The final act seemed to transfix the audience.
The children stood transfixed by the bright fireworks.

definition: to change the order or position of two or more things

collocations.example: It is easy to transpose two letters when typing fast.
Please transpose the order of these two paragraphs.

definition: the outward signs or objects associated with a status or position

collocations.example: He loved the trappings of power more than the duties.
She cared little for the outward trappings of success.

definition: a group or set of three related people or things

collocations.example: The plan rests on a triad of goals.
These three rules form a triad of core values.

definition: a group of three related books, films, or plays

collocations.example: The director finished his epic film trilogy.
She hopes to complete a trilogy of novels.

definition: a three-legged stand used to support a camera or other equipment

collocations.example: She steadied the shot with a camera tripod.
The camera sat securely on a tripod.

definition: a student who stays away from school without permission

collocations.example: He became a habitual truant in his last year.
A truant officer visited the boy's home.

definition: a framework of beams that supports a roof, bridge, or other structure

collocations.example: Carpenters lifted each wooden roof truss into place.
The bridge rests on a massive steel truss.

definition: a very large ocean wave caused by an earthquake or volcano under the sea

collocations.example: Officials issued a tsunami warning after the quake.
A landslide could trigger a tsunami here.

definition: shaped like a tube; long, round, and hollow

collocations.example: The stem has a hollow tubular structure.
The chair uses a frame of tubular steel.

definition: a brightly colored, cup-shaped spring flower grown from a bulb

collocations.example: She planted each tulip bulb before winter.
We walked past a field of tulips in bloom.

definition: a device that uses exhaust gases to boost an engine's power; a turbocharger

collocations.example: The sports car has a powerful turbo engine.
The mechanic will fit a turbo to boost power.

definition: a round, pale root vegetable eaten as food

collocations.example: We served the beef with a bowl of mashed turnip.
Heavy rain ruined the farmer's turnip crop.

definition: (of birds) to make a series of short, high sounds

collocations.example: Small birds twitter in the hedge at dawn.
The finches twitter away happily in the trees.

definition: a very wealthy and powerful person in business

collocations.example: The hotel was bought by a business tycoon.
She became a self-made tycoon by forty.

definition: a final demand that carries a threat if it is not accepted

collocations.example: The union may issue an ultimatum to managers.
She gave him a final ultimatum about the mess.

definition: the lowest social group, often poor and lacking opportunities

collocations.example: Unemployment created a growing underclass in the city.
The report described a trapped urban underclass.

definition: the bushes and small plants that grow beneath larger trees

collocations.example: The trail vanished into dense undergrowth.
A deer crashed through the undergrowth.

definition: a person whose job is to arrange funerals and prepare bodies for burial

collocations.example: The family had to call the undertaker that night.
A local undertaker arranged the whole funeral.

definition: to think that someone or something is worth less than they really are

collocations.example: Buyers often undervalue a property before bidding.
Managers should never undervalue someone's work.
